A_target.statement:
Let $N$ be a [[Definition:Flow Network|flow network]] with source $s$ and sink $t$.
Then:
:$\max \set {\size f: f \text { an } s \text {-} t \text { flow} } = \min \set {\map c S: S \text { an } s \text {-} t \text { cut} }$

B_source.statement:
Let a [[Definition:Linear Program|linear program]] and its [[Definition:Dual Linear Program|dual]] both be [[Definition:Feasible Solution|feasible]].
Then their optimal values are equal.

substitutions.the primal LP: the max-flow linear program (maximize flow subject to capacity and conservation)
substitutions.the dual LP: an LP whose integral optima are s-t cuts

derived.integrality of the flow/cut polytopes: the LP optima are achieved at integer flows and genuine cuts

object_map.reformulation: Formulate max-flow as a linear program; its dual encodes cuts, and total unimodularity makes the optima integral.

validity_conditions: Max-flow is a linear program; its dual variables (on edges/vertices) describe s-t cuts.
Strong LP duality equates the two optimal values.
The constraint matrix is totally unimodular, so both optima are attained at integer points - an actual flow and an actual cut - giving max flow = min cut.
proof_plan: Write max-flow as a [[Definition:Linear Program|linear program]]: maximize the net flow out of $s$ subject to $0 \le f_e \le c_e$ and [[Definition:Flow Conservation|conservation]] at every vertex other than $s$ and $t$.

Form the [[Definition:Dual Linear Program|dual]]: minimize $\displaystyle \sum_e c_e d_e$ subject to potentials $p$ with $p_s - p_t \ge 1$ and $d_{u v} \ge p_u - p_v$, $d \ge 0$.
Its integral solutions with $p \in \set {0, 1}$ are exactly the indicator vectors of $s$-$t$ cuts.
By the [[Strong Duality Theorem]], the primal and dual optima are equal.
